blocks.text: Mastering Chrome shortcuts for clinical speed

Your time is better spent on accuracy than on clicking menus. Chrome for medical transcriptionists on Mac works best when you keep your hands on the keyboard. Use ⌘ + T to open a new tab instantly. If you have too many tabs open, press ⌘ + Option + Right Arrow to cycle through them. You can jump directly to a specific tab using ⌘ + 1 through ⌘ + 8. This helps when you need to switch between an EHR dashboard and a medical dictionary site.

Privacy and focus are vital. Create a dedicated Chrome profile for your work tasks. Go to the Profile icon in the top right corner, then select Add to create a new profile. This keeps your work cookies, history, and bookmarks separate from your personal browsing. It also ensures that a stray personal tab does not interfere with the performance of your clinical documentation software.

items: Limit your active extensions to those you use every hour.
Clear your cache via Chrome > Clear Browsing Data if the browser feels sluggish.
Check your memory usage in Window > Task Manager to identify heavy tabs.
Restart Chrome at the end of each shift to clear out background processes.

blocks.text: If a specific site is acting up, you can clear data for just that domain. Go to Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > View permissions and data stored across sites.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to speed up documentation

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you stay in the flow. When you are working in Chrome, hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you are stuck on a complex medical term, ask Lazur to explain it. You can also use the dictation feature by holding the fn key to enter text directly into your EHR fields. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on the document.
Common mistakes in clinical browser use

Many professionals let their browser history grow too large. This can slow down your Mac over time. Set a routine to clear your cache once a week. Another mistake is leaving resource-intensive web apps open in the background. If you are not using a tab, close it with ⌘ + W. If you need to save it for later, use the bookmark feature with ⌘ + D.

Transcription work requires high concentration. Take a short break every hour to stretch. Use your Mac to set timers or reminders. You can ask Lazur to set a timer for 10 minutes when you need a quick reset. This helps prevent fatigue and keeps your accuracy high throughout the day.

faq.question: Can I use Chrome extensions for medical transcription?
faq.answer: Yes, but be careful. Only install extensions from trusted sources. Too many extensions can cause Chrome to crash or slow down.

faq.question: How do I fix a slow browser on Mac?
faq.answer: First, check for updates in Chrome > About Google Chrome. Then, clear your browsing data and remove unused extensions.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with my EHR in Chrome?
faq.answer: Lazur works on your Mac screen. You can use it to dictate text into any field in Chrome or to ask questions about the information displayed on your screen.
